$comment:
Reference budget: audits apps/storefront, which scripts/strip-reference.mjs deletes. This file leaves with it -- see sentra.referenceConfigs in the root package.json. Same maxNumericValue-only limitation as lighthouserc.json's $comment: this file cannot assert a resource floor (@lhci/cli 0.15.1 has no minNumericValue), so an empty apps/storefront/dist would pass every assertion here. That floor is enforced two ways: (1) the `lighthouse` CI job's own `Check bundle sizes` step (pnpm verify:bundle-size), which runs immediately after this job's VITE_SENTRA_MOCKS=true build and before either Lighthouse invocation, protecting the exact tree this file measures; and (2), new in fix round 2, `domSizeFloor` below plus scripts/check-lighthouse-dom-floor.mjs (wired into verify:lighthouse:reference in package.json) -- see the ROUTE FIX and DOM-SIZE FLOOR notes. ROUTE FIX (item 1, fix round 2): the second URL was http://127.0.0.1:4173/collections/all, which is not a route this app defines. apps/storefront/src/federated/routes.ts declares exactly two paths -- '' (the collection/home view) and 'products/:handle' -- so `/collections/all` matched neither; Vue Router's `` rendered nothing for it. This was NOT a `vite preview` static-file-serving or SPA-history-fallback defect as first hypothesised: the document request itself returned HTTP 200 and every other asset on that path returned 200 too (confirmed via the network-requests audit); the router simply had no route to match, which is a client-side condition a working server-level fallback cannot fix. The measured page was 9 DOM elements (header + empty
) scoring a perfect 1.0 on accessibility -- a confident green number for a page that does not exist. Replaced with http://127.0.0.1:4173/products/sentra-piece-2, a real product detail route (sentra-piece-1 was passed over deliberately: its fixture carries a hostile-content probe, HOSTILE_DESCRIPTION, unrepresentative of a normal budget baseline). Confirmed by DOM size: the corrected page measures 22 elements, not 9. IMAGE FIX (item 2, fix round 2): the storefront home page previously showed 20 failed resource loads. Root cause, confirmed via the network-requests and errors-in-console audits: apps/storefront/src/components/ProductGrid.vue calls the real `shopifyImageUrl`/`shopifyImageSrcset` helpers (packages/sdk-commerce/src/images.ts), genuine production code that builds real `https://cdn.shopify.com/...` URLs -- and packages/sdk-commerce/src/mocks/handlers.ts had no handler for image requests at all, only for the Storefront GraphQL endpoint. Every image request fell through MSW to the real network and 404'd against a hostname these fixtures do not own. This was NOT 'MSW forcing image bytes to 0' as originally (and incorrectly) documented -- at the time of that claim the images were not mocked at all. Fixed by adding an `http.get` handler for the fixture image URL pattern in handlers.ts, returning a hand-built, deterministic 150x150 PNG (packages/sdk-commerce/src/mocks/fixtures.ts's MOCK_PRODUCT_IMAGE_BASE64 -- there is no image library or real photo asset anywhere in this repo). Confirmed fixed: the network-requests audit now shows all 20 (home) / 1 (product page) image requests at statusCode 200, mimeType image/png, resourceSize 11387 -- a real, correctly-served response, not a 404. image:size (500000) is STILL a placeholder, but the reason changed and is now independently verified rather than assumed. resource-summary:image:size sums `transferSize`, and a Service Worker's `respondWith()` response is synthesised in-process -- it never crosses Chrome's real network transport, so DevTools reports transferSize 0 for it regardless of content. Confirmed directly: the same corrected, successfully-served image request that shows statusCode 200 and resourceSize 11387 (its real decoded byte count) also shows transferSize 0 in the identical network-requests entry. This is a property of MSW interception itself, not of these particular images being broken or empty -- it would be 0 for a correct 1-byte fixture or a correct 10MB one alike. Raising this to a live, meaningful ceiling requires a non-mocked reference build, which is out of this task's scope; 500000 remains an explicit, labelled, CANNOT-FAIL-TODAY placeholder, not a passing budget with a live signal. third-party:count (22, home page, still the worse of the two URLs) is set to the exact measured value, investigated rather than raised blind: 2 GraphQL calls to demo-shop.myshopify.com plus 20 product-image calls to cdn.shopify.com, every one intercepted by MSW at transferSize 0 for the reason above -- the mock fixtures use realistic external hostnames instead of same-origin paths, so Lighthouse's third-party classifier fires on the hostname even though zero bytes cross the wire in either direction. Known property of the mock harness, not a live third-party dependency; still catches a genuinely new third-party request immediately. RE-DERIVED BASELINE (item 2, fix round 2, re-measured 2026-08-30 after the route and image fixes above, numberOfRuns=3, worst-of-3 per URL): http://127.0.0.1:4173/ -- dom-size 183, total 327623B/49 requests, script 321570B/25, stylesheet 5092B/1, document 961B/1, image 0B/20 (see note above), third-party 0B/22, LCP 1205.57ms, TBT 0ms, CLS 0.2960, accessibility 0.98, best-practices 0.96; http://127.0.0.1:4173/products/sentra-piece-2 -- dom-size 22, total 327623B/29, script 321570B/25, stylesheet 5092B/1, image 0B/1, third-party 0B/2, LCP 997.73ms, TBT 0ms, CLS 0, accessibility 1.0, best-practices 0.96. Every budget below uses the worse of the two URLs. script:size (321570 measured) has grown from the prior 309480B baseline: the new MOCK_PRODUCT_IMAGE_BASE64 fixture is committed source, not a static asset, so its ~15KB base64 string is bundled directly into the mocks chunk. script:size (354816) and stylesheet:size (5632, unchanged) use bundle-budgets.json's own convention (round the measured byte count up to the next whole KB, then +10%): ceil(321570/1024)=315KB, 322560*1.10=354816. total:size (863516) is the sum of the per-type ceilings (354816+5632+500000) plus the same ~3068B allowance for unbudgeted document/other categories the prior baseline used, so it cannot become the binding constraint ahead of a dedicated per-type budget. largest-contentful-paint (1400ms) is measured+15% off the worse URL's 1205.57ms, rounded up to the nearest 50ms: 1205.57*1.15=1386.4. total-blocking-time (50ms) mirrors the shell's deliberate CI-noise tolerance. cumulative-layout-shift (0.35) is unchanged: the re-measured home-page value (0.2960) is materially identical to the prior baseline (0.296) -- this layout shift is real, pre-existing, and untouched by the route/image fixes (the product-image has an explicit h-40 fixed-height container, so it was never the source); fixing it remains out of Task 8's scope and stays flagged as a follow-up. ACCESSIBILITY PIN RE-VERIFIED, NOT REMOVED (item 3, fix round 2): re-checked against the corrected, correctly-rendering home page rather than the old broken one. It did NOT return to 1.0 -- it re-measured at the identical 0.98, and this time the cause is directly confirmed from the Lighthouse accessibility audit's own per-audit breakdown, not inferred: `heading-order` is the ONLY sub-audit scoring below 1 (score 0), flagging one specific node, `div.h-full > article.overflow-hidden > button.focus-visible:outline > h3.text-sm` (a ProductCard title) as not sequentially preceded by a valid ancestor heading. Every other accessibility sub-audit scores 1. This closes the exact gap fix round 1 left open: the 0.98 pin is not carrying forward a defect that might have been the 20 broken images in disguise -- it is now shown, on a page with zero broken resources, to be heading-order and only heading-order. The 'Known issues carried forward to Task 14' entry in task-8-report.md is therefore CONFIRMED, not retracted; categories:accessibility (minScore 0.98) reflects a real, reproducible, now doubly-verified defect, not a looser standard for its own sake. Setting minScore to 1 would make this gate permanently red for a pre-existing markup defect unrelated to Task 8's scope; fixing the heading order and raising this to 1 remains the flagged follow-up. DOM-SIZE FLOOR (item 5, fix round 2): `domSizeFloor` below (checked by scripts/check-lighthouse-dom-floor.mjs, wired into verify:lighthouse:reference in package.json) sets the lower bound `lhci` cannot express. Home page floor (100) sits well below its measured 183 and well above every broken-page reading seen in this task (9 elements, both for the old `/collections/all` route miss and, in the shell's sibling config, its own failure class). Product-page floor (15) sits between its measured 22 and that same 9-element broken-page reading -- tighter headroom than the home page's because the page itself is smaller, but still strictly above the proven-broken class.
